subject: Energy
title: ITER and Tokamaks
description: A short lesson to help you apply ITER and Tokamaks.

hook.text: ITER is the world's largest fusion experiment—under construction in France, backed by 35 nations.

buildup.text: It uses a tokamak design—a doughnut-shaped chamber where powerful magnets confine 150-million-degree plasma.

discovery.text: ITER aims to produce 500 MW of fusion power from 50 MW of input—a tenfold energy gain, proving fusion is viable.

twist.text: ITER won't generate electricity—it's a science experiment. A follow-up reactor (DEMO) would be the first power plant.

climax.text: The project has faced decades of delays and cost overruns—originally planned for 2016, now targeting the early 2030s.

punchline.text: The biggest science experiment ever—still chasing the Sun.

quiz.question: What shape is a tokamak fusion reactor?
